newsitem.title: KENYA: Industrial firms help Nairobi bourse index up.
newsitem.headline: Industrial firms help Nairobi bourse index up.

text.p: Big lots traded in Bamburi Cement and high value shares of power distribution monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting boosted the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index on Monday, brokers said.
The index gained 9.34 points to close at 3055.89. Turnover was posted at 7.205 million shillings traded on 194,345 shares from 9.937 million shillings traded on 614,678 shares.

Bamburi traded 45,500 shares at 29 from 28 while foreigners bought a single lot of 10,000 shares of Kenya Power & Lighting Co at 124 from 122. Some 3,300 shares of Total Kenya were traded at 69 from 70 previously.
Bamburi and East African Portland Cement are the only listed companies that manufacture and sell cement and are also the leading distributors for the whole of East Africa.

"Bamburi is at least assured of a ready market, in fact about 50 percent of its cement is for the export market," a broker said. "There is absolutely no way the two companies can service the demand for cement in the region," he added.
There has been sustained interest in Kenya Power & Lighting shares from foreigners over the last two weeks.
In the financials, National Bank of Kenya traded 1,450 shares at 14.55 from 14.30, Standard Chartered Bank traded 3,150 shares at 46.25 from 46.
National Bank of Kenya announced an interim dividend of 75 cents on Nov 1. Brokers said investors were expecting the announcement and appeared pleased with the interim dividend.
They said the same could hardly be said for the announcement by Industrial Investment for Commercial Development (ICDC) which announced a final dividend of 2.50. It's price eased to 35.25 from 36.25.
Kapchorua Tea dealt 3,266 shares at 96.50 from 96, while Uchumi Supermarkets traded 8,550 shares at 50 from 51.
